metadata.rules_text:
- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% if recent price surged.
- Underestimates mean-reversion zones; if sentiment is neutral or negative, adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Overshoots after volatility spikes (e.g., 80+ → 85+), then corrects; apply “cool-down” rule: subtract 2–3% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance; cap forecast range within ±3% of 14-day moving average to reduce noise.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after forecast peak, apply “reversion bias” correction: reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5 days if sentiment remains neutral.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle corrections; add 1–2% downward adjustment if true outcome shows 3+ consecutive days of decline.
